62846250
If you go 100% bonds,
and long duration,
you have extreme interest rate risk
we could be looking at future financial repression,
and interest rates hitting 15% or higher depending on how bad the debt crisis gets. The debt crisis which s coming to a head in the mid 2030s. That would fuck you. Don't go long duration. Short duration only, but the yield on short duration isn't as much as long.

If you really just have to have your bonds do,

50% BNDW
25% FNDX
25% FNDF

That gives you 50% global bonds, and you don't have geographic risk
it gives you 50% equities each weighted on fundamentals. Or instead of FNDX and FNDF you could go for memes like VOO and SCHD because people suck the dicks of those funds. FNDF and FNDX weight companies based on fundamentals. It's a defensive allocation strategy, and biases yield as well. FNDX and FNDF won't chase some meme stock and instead allocate the funds into cash monsters.

Very low vol portfolio, very conservative, and low risk,
and enough equities to have capital appreciation.Yield chasing portfolio.

Have at least some equities, even if you're 70 years old, always have some. It reduces risk. Bonds and equities are negatively correlated, but bonds, whether they're sovereign bonds, US bonds, corporate bonds are all correlated with other bonds. So if this bond bear market continues, you're going to feel the pain no matter whether you're all US treasurys, or world bonds. Diversifying your bonds reduces the pain.
